scope: Independent audit of stocks mentioned in the Sep 3 creator briefs. Creator technical levels, option-flow claims and correlation narratives are discovery inputs only and receive zero direct Power Stack score weight until verified.
regime: Refined-product inflation + global long-end yield stress + softer hiring + selective industrial/AI physical capex. This favours pricing power, domestic scarcity and cash-generative balance sheets while penalising fuel-sensitive transport and distant-duration/pre-commercial equities.

verdicts.name: Cleveland-Cliffs
verdicts.verdict: PROMOTE TO SELECTIVE RESEARCH / BUY RETEST
verdicts.fit: High tactical regime fit, medium business quality
verdicts.why: Q2 adjusted EBITDA improved to $286m from $95m in Q1, operating cash flow turned positive, management expects about $575m Q3 adjusted EBITDA, imports remain subdued and domestic demand/lead times are improving. The current US steel/tariff backdrop adds cyclical torque.
verdicts.risk: Leveraged, cyclical and less structurally clean than NUE/STLD. Do not chase a one-day tariff/steel-price squeeze.
verdicts.action: Prefer a retest after the Sep 2 surge; promote the US steel-protection/reindustrialisation theme and compare CLF against NUE/STLD before any core upgrade.

verdicts.name: Wells Fargo
verdicts.verdict: PROMOTE TO SELECTIVE RESEARCH / BREAKOUT-RETEST WATCH
verdicts.fit: Good higher-for-longer fit while credit remains controlled
verdicts.why: Q2 net income was $6.4b, revenue $22.6b, NII $12.3b, average loans +12% YoY and deposits +10%. ROE reached 15% while net charge-offs and CRE nonperformers improved.
verdicts.risk: Higher rates are not automatically bullish forever. If funding costs, delinquencies, CRE/consumer credit or loan demand deteriorate, the same yield regime becomes a headwind.
verdicts.action: Add to the bank/curve watch. Prefer retest or confirmed breakout rather than chasing a strong single session.

verdicts.name: Mastercard
verdicts.fit: Excellent company, only moderate current macro edge
verdicts.why: Q2 net revenue rose 14% to $9.3b; purchase volume +10%, cross-border volume +12%, switched transactions +9%, and value-added services +20%. The business remains exceptionally high quality.
verdicts.risk: Near-high valuation plus consumer/travel sensitivity means the current yield/energy squeeze offers less asymmetry than scarcity infrastructure or banks.
verdicts.action: Research-quality compounder, but no forced entry. Promote only on a better valuation/price reset or a stronger cross-border/consumer setup.

verdicts.name: The Trade Desk
verdicts.verdict: TURNAROUND WATCH / DO NOT PROMOTE YET
verdicts.fit: Damaged growth turnaround, not a macro winner
verdicts.why: Q2 revenue grew only 3% to $715m while adjusted EBITDA fell to $241m from $271m and adjusted EBITDA margin compressed to 34% from 39%. Management explicitly said the quarter did not meet its standard.
verdicts.risk: High yields, software/private-credit stress and weak execution outweigh the optional benefit from platform-antitrust pressure on Amazon. An FTC lawsuit is not a direct earnings catalyst for TTD.
verdicts.action: Keep as a research-only turnaround. Require revenue and margin reacceleration before Power Stack promotion.

verdicts.name: Palantir
verdicts.verdict: EXCEPTIONAL FUNDAMENTALS / WRONG REGIME TO CHASE
verdicts.fit: Fundamental quality high; duration/valuation sensitivity high
verdicts.why: Q2 revenue grew 93% to $1.935b, US commercial revenue +149%, GAAP operating margin 47% and adjusted FCF $1.22b. Full-year revenue and FCF guidance were raised materially.
verdicts.risk: The business is executing far better than most software peers, but the current long-yield regime makes very high valuation multiples unusually vulnerable to compression.
verdicts.action: Do not short the business thesis; do not chase the multiple. Reassess after a deeper valuation reset or durable 10Y/real-yield relief.

verdicts.name: United Airlines
verdicts.fit: Wrong side of the refined-product shock
verdicts.why: United produced $17.7b Q2 revenue and $322m FCF with $19.6b liquidity, so the company is not broken. But Q2 average fuel cost was already $4.19/gal and the current jet-fuel/refining shock raises the cost hurdle sharply.
verdicts.risk: Jet fuel and Middle East disruption can overwhelm otherwise healthy demand. Airlines are also exposed to consumer/travel weakening.
verdicts.action: Do not promote while product cracks remain extreme. A durable oil/jet-fuel rollover is the clean confirmation for a better airline setup.

verdicts.name: Rigetti Computing
verdicts.why: Q2 revenue was just $5.1m against a $28.1m operating loss and $52.6m GAAP net loss. The positive is $541.3m of cash/investments and no debt, which gives the technology roadmap runway.
verdicts.risk: Commercial revenue remains tiny relative to market expectations. Option flow or a historical bounce from support does not fix the duration/valuation mismatch.
verdicts.action: No Power Stack core promotion. Revisit only on material commercial revenue, useful-system milestones and a less hostile discount-rate regime.

verdicts.name: Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund
verdicts.fit: Strong current macro fit, redundant with existing energy exposure
verdicts.why: Brent around $95.6, WTI around $91, 98% US refinery utilisation and extreme gasoline/diesel cracks keep energy earnings support strong.
verdicts.risk: War premium and demand destruction can reverse quickly. The user already owns XOM and HIBISCS, so generic XLE adds overlap rather than a new edge.
verdicts.action: Prefer existing integrated exposure or targeted refining/product bottleneck names such as VLO/MPC/PSX rather than adding XLE solely because energy is leading.
